newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bits and pieces proffered.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bits and pieces proffered.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a little of this and a little of that on Wednesday.
Details emerged on a few new issues.
Korea Exchange Bank's debut Kangaroo bond will be offered to investors on December 10 via lead manager Bankers Trust Australia.
The three-year bonds will be priced to yield 37-40 basis points over comparable Australian government bonds.
The KEB issue is the second Kangaroo bond offered to Australian investors and the first to be launched since a relaxation in government rules on foreign banks' domestic securities issues.
Quasi-sovereign Korea Development Bank launched a A$150 million Kangaroo bond in August via lead manager Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Bankers said the KEB issue will pay a margin of 25-26 basis points over London Interbank Offered Rate on an asset-swap basis.

As for other South Korean issues, rumours continued to fly on a suspected issue for Korea Electric Power Co, which has been variously reported as a Yankee bond, a dollar Eurobond or a deutschmark bond.
Samsung Electronics Co is slated to launch a 300 million mark five-year bond via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell on Thursday.
Elsewhere, Philippines Airlines has mandated AB Capital Markets and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to arrange a US$100 million floating rate note issue.
The three-year notes will be formally launched on December 4. They will be priced at par to pay a coupon of 200 basis points over LIBOR and, with fees, an all-in return of 225 basis points.
Roadshows are being held this week in Asia for a US$100 million 144a Eurobond for Universal Robina, which is largely held by Philippines company JG Summit. Merrill Lynch reportedly is the lead.

National Power Corp has filed a shelf offering with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for up to US$200 million in bonds. Napocor's long-awaited Yankee bond could launch before year-end. Salomon Brothers is lead manager.

Comments by Philippines central bank governor Gabriel Singson earlier this month that the country would consider issuing a 30-year bond have spurred speculation that a mandate could be in the offing soon.
